newsitem.title: USA: Woman indicted in Cosby extortion case.
newsitem.headline: Woman indicted in Cosby extortion case.

text.p: A federal grand jury on Thursday indicted a woman who claimed to be Bill Cosby's illegitimate daughter, saying she tried to extort $40 million from the entertainer.

Federal prosecutors said Autumn Jackson, 22, and her alleged accomplice, Jose Medina, 51, were named in a three-count indictment alleging they tried to obtain money from Cosby by threatening to reveal to a tabloid newpaper Jackson's claim she was Cosby's out-of-wedlock daughter.
They were charged with conspiracy, extortion and violating the federal law that prohibits people from travelling in interstate commerce to commit certain offences.
If convicted of all counts, they face a possible total prison term of 12 years and fines of $750,000.

Cosby has admitted to having an affair with Jackson's mother but denied being her father. According to court papers, Jackson was one of many young people for whom Cosby paid educational expenses for several years.
Federal prosecutors have said there was no evidence the scheme was connected to the murder of Cosby's son, Ennis, killed in Los Angeles on Jan 16.
The indictment charges that Jackson and Medina tried to pressure Cosby to turn over the money by contacting Cosby's corporate sponsors and the CBS television network, which broadcasts his programme.

According to the indictment, Jackson sent a letter to Cosby's lawyer on Jan. 16 stating, "I need monies and I need monies now" and that "I don't want to do anything to harm my father in any way, if at all possible to avoid."
The indictment alleges she spoke to the lawyer on Jan. 17 and demanded $40 million. She eventually agreed not to make her claim in exchange for $24 million.

The two defendants flew to New York on the night of Jan. 17 and met with the lawyer the next morning. They were arrested after they signed an agreement stating they would not sell Jackson's story in exchange for $24 million.
Jackson was released on bail on Jan. 28 but Medina remained in custody.
